mainTopic: Who wrote the משנה on meat and milk and on vowing off meat? Is עוף in milk forbidden by the Torah?
overview: The משנה ends by saying that someone who vows off meat may still eat fish and grasshoppers. The גמרא infers from the earlier part of the משנה that עוף cooked in milk is forbidden מדאורייתא. That part cannot follow רבי עקיבא, who holds that חיה ועוף in milk are only rabbinic. But the vow line implies that birds count as meat. That fits רבי עקיבא's rule that anything an agent would ask about belongs to the category, which comes from his argument with the חכמים about gourds and vegetables. So the משנה seems split between the רבנן and רבי עקיבא. רב יוסף answers that רבי followed different opinions for different topics. רב אשי answers that the whole משנה is רבי עקיבא, since its meat-and-milk ban includes both Torah-level and rabbinic cases. Then רב יוסף proves from the ban on placing bird meat on the table with cheese that עוף in milk is Torah-forbidden, because the חכמים do not make a decree on top of a decree. The גמרא starts to bring a source for that rule from חלה outside ארץ ישראל, and the proof continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The last line of the משנה: vowing off meat
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that a person who takes a נדר against meat may still eat fish and grasshoppers.
steps.simpleTranslation: Someone who vows not to eat meat is still allowed to eat the meat of fish and grasshoppers.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last line of the משנה. It tells us that a נדר against "meat" does not include fish or grasshoppers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A נדר follows how people normally talk. People do not call fish or grasshoppers "meat," so they are not covered. The משנה is silent about birds, and the גמרא will soon draw a conclusion from that silence.

keyTerms.meaning: One who takes a vow (נדר) forbidding something to himself
Meat
Fish and grasshoppers (kosher locusts)

phrases.english: One who vows off meat
is permitted to eat the meat of fish and grasshoppers.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַנּוֹדֵר מִן הַבָּשָׂר מוּתָּר בִּבְשַׂר דָּגִים וַחֲגָבִים
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A vow against meat does not include fish or grasshoppers.

steps.title: Birds are forbidden by Torah law: whose view is that?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers from the משנה that עוף cooked in milk is forbidden מדאורייתא, and asks which תנא holds this.
steps.simpleTranslation: The גמרא begins: this implies that bird meat is forbidden with milk by Torah law. Whose opinion is that?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws an inference from the משנה and asks who its author is. It is setting up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier part of the משנה said all meat is forbidden to cook in milk except fish and grasshoppers. Since only those two are left out, birds are included, and on the same Torah level as animal meat. Not every תנא agrees, so the גמרא asks whose view this is.

keyTerms.meaning: This implies; it follows that (introduces an inference)
Bird / fowl
By Torah law
Like whom? (Whose opinion is this?)

steps.confusionAlert: This inference is about the earlier part of the משנה (meat and milk), not about vows. The vow line is discussed only in step 4.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
This implies that bird is forbidden by Torah law,
phrases.notes: He means bird meat cooked in milk. Only fish and grasshoppers were left out, so birds count as meat here.

phrases.english: in accordance with whom?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the text of the משנה to identifying its author.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that עוף in milk is forbidden מדאורייתא?

steps.title: Not רבי עקיבא, who says birds are not Torah-forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that this part of the משנה cannot follow רבי עקיבא, because he holds that חיה ועוף in milk are not forbidden by the Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: It does not follow רבי עקיבא. If it were רבי עקיבא, he holds that wild animals and birds with milk are not forbidden by the Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question: this part of the משנה is not רבי עקיבא's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא limits the Torah prohibition of meat and milk to domestic animals. For him, birds and wild animals are forbidden only by the Rabbis. So a משנה that makes birds forbidden by the Torah cannot be his.

keyTerms.meaning: A wild (non-domesticated) animal, such as a deer
Is not from the Torah (only a rabbinic prohibition)
But he said! (points out a known contrary opinion)

phrases.english: Not in accordance with רבי עקיבא,
for if it were רבי עקיבא, didn't he say:
wild animal and bird are not forbidden by the Torah.
phrases.notes: This is about cooking them in milk. For רבי עקיבא, that prohibition is only from the Rabbis.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּלָא כְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא, דְּאִי רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא הָאָמַר
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The earlier part of the משנה is not רבי עקיבא, since he says חיה ועוף in milk are only rabbinic.

steps.title: But the last line of the משנה does follow רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads the vow clause. Since only fish and grasshoppers are permitted, birds are forbidden, which matches רבי עקיבא's rule that whatever an agent would ask about counts as part of the category.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now look at the last line: one who vows off meat may eat fish and grasshoppers. That implies birds are forbidden. That brings us to רבי עקיבא, who said: anything an agent would ask about counts as the same kind.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a problem. The earlier part of the משנה is not רבי עקיבא, but the last line seems to be רבי עקיבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Picture an agent sent to buy meat who finds only chicken. He would ask, "Should I get chicken?" For רבי עקיבא, the very fact that he would ask shows chicken belongs to the "meat" category, so a vow against meat forbids birds. That means one משנה would have two different authors, and that is the difficulty.

keyTerms.meaning: Say the latter part (now look at the end of the משנה)
We have arrived at (this fits the opinion of...)
Consults / asks for instructions
Agent / messenger
Of its kind (belongs to the same category)

steps.whyThisMatters: This rule, that a vow covers anything an agent would ask about, is רבי עקיבא's main principle for how far a נדר reaches.

phrases.english: Say the latter clause:
One who vows off meat
is permitted to eat the meat of fish and grasshoppers,
this implies bird is forbidden,
we have arrived at רבי עקיבא, who said:
anything about which an agent would ask
is considered its kind.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets the last line of the משנה (רבי עקיבא) against the earlier part (not רבי עקיבא).
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that the whole משנה has one author.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The earlier part cannot be רבי עקיבא, but the last line fits only רבי עקיבא's agent rule. So the משנה seems to have two authors.

steps.title: Source for רבי עקיבא's rule: vowing off vegetables
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא: one who vows off vegetables may eat gourds, but רבי עקיבא forbids them.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: one who vows off vegetables is allowed to eat gourds, but רבי עקיבא forbids them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source that shows where רבי עקיבא's agent rule comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים say gourds are not normally called "vegetables," so they are permitted. רבי עקיבא forbids them, because gourds are close enough to vegetables that an agent would ask about them.

keyTerms.meaning: Vegetables
Gourds (squash-type produce)
Forbids

phrases.english: As it is taught:
One who vows off vegetables
is permitted to eat gourds,
but רבי עקיבא forbids them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the רבי עקיבא principle cited in step 4.
steps.raayaObject: רבי עקיבא's rule that whatever an agent would ask about is part of the category.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about a vow against vegetables, where רבי עקיבא forbids gourds.

steps.title: The חכמים challenge רבי עקיבא from the agent's words
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים argue that an agent sent for vegetables says "I found only gourds," which shows gourds are not vegetables.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to רבי עקיבא: But a person tells his agent, "Buy us vegetables," and the agent comes back and says, "I only found gourds!"
steps.whatsHappening: Still inside the ברייתא, the חכמים push back on רבי עקיבא. His reply comes right after this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים point to the agent's wording. He says he did not find vegetables, only gourds, so gourds must be something other than vegetables. The same agent scene is what רבי עקיבא's principle is built on.

keyTerms.meaning: But is it not so that... (opens a challenge)
His agent
I found only...

steps.confusionAlert: This is the חכמים speaking, not רבי עקיבא. Right after this, רבי עקיבא answers using the very same agent scene.

phrases.english: They said to רבי עקיבא:
But doesn't a person say to his agent:
"Buy us vegetables,"
and he says:
"I found only gourds!"

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ לְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא: וַהֲלֹא אוֹמֵר אָדָם לִשְׁלוּחוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Inside the quoted ברייתא, the חכמים challenge רבי עקיבא's ruling from step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי עקיבא's ruling that gourds are included in a vow against vegetables.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The agent says "I found only gourds," which treats gourds as separate from vegetables, so they should not be covered by the vow.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא turns the agent argument around
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא answers the חכמים: the agent asks about gourds, but never about legumes, so gourds really are part of the vegetable category.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: That is exactly my point! Would the agent ever say "I only found legumes"? No. So gourds are part of "vegetables", and legumes are not.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא answers the חכמים from the last step. He uses their own example of the agent to prove his side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים said the agent's words "I only found gourds" show that gourds are separate from vegetables. רבי עקיבא says the opposite: the agent bothers to mention gourds at all only because they belong to the vegetable family. He would never mention legumes, which truly are a different category.

keyTerms.meaning: Legumes (beans, lentils and the like)
Gourds
Included in the category of vegetables

steps.confusionAlert: Both sides use the exact same agent example. The חכמים read it as proof that gourds are separate. רבי עקיבא reads it as proof that gourds are included. Don't mix up who says what.

phrases.english: He said to them: That is exactly the point;
phrases.notes: "He" is רבי עקיבא, still speaking inside the ברייתא.

phrases.english: does the agent ever say "I found only legumes"?!
Rather, this shows that gourds are included in vegetables,
but legumes are not included in vegetables.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the חכמים' argument from step 6 inside the same ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The agent's question shows gourds are not vegetables
steps.terutzMaskana: The agent asks about gourds only because they are part of the vegetable category

steps.title: The משנה seems split between two opinions
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes the difficulty: the meat-and-milk clause follows the רבנן, but the vow clause follows רבי עקיבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: So the first part of the משנה follows the רבנן, and the last part follows רבי עקיבא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states the problem that steps 2 through 7 were building up to. The one משנה seems to follow two different opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first clause treats עוף in milk as forbidden by the Torah, which fits the רבנן and not רבי עקיבא. The vow clause counts birds as "meat" because an agent would ask about them, which is רבי עקיבא's rule from the gourd ברייתא. An unexplained split like this is a difficulty that needs an answer.

keyTerms.meaning: The first clause of a משנה
The last clause of a משנה

phrases.english: The first clause follows the Rabbis,
phrases.notes: The first clause is the meat-and-milk part, where birds seem forbidden by the Torah.

phrases.english: and the last clause follows Rabbi Akiva!
phrases.notes: The last clause is the vow part, which counts birds as meat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion of the proof from the ברייתא
steps.kashyaTarget: The unity of the משנה's authorship
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two clauses of one משנה seem to follow opposing תנאים

steps.title: רב יוסף: רבי chose different opinions for different topics
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says the author is רבי, who followed רבי עקיבא on vows and the רבנן on meat and milk.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: The משנה is רבי's. He arranged it according to different תנאים. On vows he holds like רבי עקיבא, and on meat and milk he holds like the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers the difficulty. He accepts that the clauses follow different opinions and explains why that is fine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is no contradiction, because the two clauses deal with two separate topics. רבי, who arranged the משנה, simply decided each topic according to the opinion he held there: רבי עקיבא for vows and the רבנן for meat and milk.

keyTerms.meaning: He arranged it according to different תנאים
Vows

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: It is Rebbi's,
and he arranges it according to different tanna'im:
regarding vows he holds like Rabbi Akiva,
regarding meat in milk he holds like the Rabbis.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributes the משנה to a single editor who followed different opinions
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One משנה cannot follow two opposing opinions
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי picked רבי עקיבא for vows and the רבנן for meat and milk

steps.title: רב אשי: The whole משנה follows רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי reads the first clause as including both Torah-level and rabbinic bans, so the whole משנה fits רבי עקיבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: The whole משנה is רבי עקיבא. This is what it means: all meat is forbidden to cook in milk, some by Torah law and some by rabbinic law. The only exception is fish and grasshoppers, which are not forbidden by either.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives a different answer to the same difficulty. He rereads the first clause so it fits רבי עקיבא too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The difficulty assumed that the first clause makes everything except fish and grasshoppers forbidden by the Torah. רב אשי says the clause only lists what is forbidden at all: animal meat by the Torah, and חיה and עוף by the חכמים. Read this way, nothing in the משנה clashes with רבי עקיבא's view that עוף in milk is not forbidden by the Torah.

keyTerms.meaning: All of it (the whole משנה)
By Torah law
By rabbinic law
Grasshoppers or locusts

steps.whatToRemember: There are two answers to the split משנה. רב יוסף says רבי mixed opinions. רב אשי says it is all רבי עקיבא, and the משנה's ban covers both Torah-level and rabbinic cases.

phrases.aramaic: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: כּוּלַּהּ רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא הִיא,
phrases.english: Rav Ashi said: The entire mishna is Rabbi Akiva's,

phrases.aramaic: וְהָכִי קָאָמַר: כׇּל הַבָּשָׂר אָסוּר לְבַשֵּׁל בְּחָלָב,
phrases.english: and this is what it is saying: all meat is forbidden to cook in milk,

phrases.aramaic: מֵהֶן מִדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה וּמֵהֶן מִדִּבְרֵי סוֹפְרִים,
phrases.english: some by Torah law and some by rabbinic law,
phrases.notes: Animal meat is the Torah-level ban; meat of a חיה and birds is the rabbinic ban.

phrases.english: except for the meat of fish and grasshoppers,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֵינָם לֹא מִדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה וְלֹא מִדִּבְרֵי סוֹפְרִים.
phrases.english: which are forbidden neither by Torah law nor by rabbinic law.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: כּוּלַּהּ רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to the same קשיא, in place of רב יוסף's
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereads the wording of the רישא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The first clause means everything except fish and grasshoppers is forbidden by the Torah
steps.terutzMaskana: The first clause covers both Torah-level and rabbinic bans, so it fits רבי עקיבא

steps.title: רב יוסף proves bird meat in milk is Torah-forbidden
steps.stepSummary: From the ban on placing meat on a table with cheese, רב יוסף proves that עוף in milk must be forbidden by the Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: "And it is forbidden to place [meat on the table with cheese]." רב יוסף said: Learn from this that bird meat in milk is forbidden by the Torah. If it were only rabbinic, then eating it would itself be a rabbinic decree. Would we then add another decree against placing it on the table, just to protect that decree?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to the next line of the משנה. רב יוסף uses it to prove that עוף in milk is a Torah-level ban.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה forbids even placing bird meat on the same table as cheese, which is a safeguard against eating them together. If eating bird meat with milk were itself only a rabbinic safeguard, this would be a safeguard on top of a safeguard, and the חכמים don't do that. So the eating ban must come from the Torah.

keyTerms.meaning: Placing (meat) up on the table together with cheese
Learn from this; a proof is being drawn
By Torah law
A protective decree made by the חכמים
Because of; out of concern for

steps.whyThisMatters: This rests on a well-known rule: the חכמים do not make one protective decree to guard another protective decree.

phrases.english: "And it is forbidden to place, etc."
phrases.notes: This quotes the next line of the משנה: you may not put meat on the table together with cheese.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: Learn from this
that bird meat in milk is forbidden by Torah law.
For if you would think it is only rabbinic,
then eating it is itself a decree,
and would we decree against placing because of eating?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next clause of the משנה and draws a new proof
steps.raayaObject: עוף in milk is forbidden by Torah law
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's ban on placing bird meat on the table with cheese, plus the rule that the חכמים don't add a decree on top of a decree

steps.title: Where do we know that there is no decree on top of a decree?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a source for the rule רב יוסף relied on: חכמים do not make a גזירה to protect another גזירה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where do you say that we do not make one rabbinic decree to protect another rabbinic decree?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to ask where we know the rule that רב יוסף's proof was built on. That rule is 'no גזירה לגזירה'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף's proof only works if חכמים never add a safety-fence around something that is already only a rabbinic fence. The גמרא is not attacking the proof. It wants a source to show the rule is real.

keyTerms.meaning: A decree on top of a decree: a rabbinic fence made to protect another rabbinic fence
We make a decree (חכמים forbid something as a protective fence)
And from where do you say this? A request for a source

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a challenge against רב יוסף. The גמרא accepts his reasoning and is only asking where the rule he used comes from.
steps.whyThisMatters: The whole proof that עוף in milk is forbidden by the Torah stands on this rule. That is why the גמרא wants a firm source for it.

phrases.english: And from where do you say
that we do not issue a decree for a decree?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמְנָא תֵּימְרָא דְּלָא גָּזְרִינַן גְּזֵירָה לִגְזֵירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the principle that רב יוסף's proof in step 11 assumed.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that חכמים do not make a גזירה to protect another גזירה.

steps.title: Opening the proof from חלה outside ארץ ישראל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins answering by quoting a משנה about חלה from outside ארץ ישראל. The proof continues in the next section.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: חלה from outside ארץ ישראל...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts bringing its source by quoting a משנה about חלה taken outside ארץ ישראל. This is only the opening words, setting up a proof that is finished in the next part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חלה from outside ארץ ישראל is itself only a rabbinic obligation, so it is a good test case for how far rabbinic fences go. The rest of the משנה will show that חכמים were lenient with it and did not add extra fences around it.

keyTerms.meaning: The portion of dough given to a כהן
Outside ארץ ישראל

phrases.english: As we learned in a mishna: ḥalla from outside the Land

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question of step 12 by citing a משנה.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that חכמים do not make a גזירה לגזירה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה חלה 4:8, about חלה from outside ארץ ישראל. Only the opening words appear here.
